function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
I’m unable to execute `git` commands or pull from an external repository directly from here, but I can give you everything you’ll need to finish the task locally.  
Below are the exact files you should create (or update) in the **root** of the cloned repository, followed by the shell commands you’ll run to stage, commit, and push your changes.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the Repository

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

> *If you’re using HTTPS instead of SSH, replace the URL with `https://github.com/zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git`.*

---

## 2️⃣ Create/Update Files

### 2.1 Dockerfile

Create a file named `Dockerfile` (no extension) with the following content:

```dockerfile
# Use the official lightweight Node.js runtime
FROM node:18-alpine

# Create app directory inside the image
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Copy dependency descriptors first
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies only
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the application
CMD ["npm", "start"]
```

> *Adjust the `EXPOSE` value if your app listens on a different port.*

---

### 2.2 Kubernetes YAML

Generate a single file called `k8s.yaml` (you can split it into separate `deployment.yaml` and `service.yaml` if you prefer).  
Because the built‑in helper only creates a generic deployment/service pair, I’ll hand‑craft the YAML to match a Node.js app:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: myregistry/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your registry/tag
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000                      # <-- adjust if needed
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> *Replace `myregistry/nodejs-welcome:latest` with the actual image name/tag you’ll push to later.*

---

### 2.3 GitHub Actions Workflow

Create a file at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with the following content:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]   # Trigger on pushes to main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'   # Match the Docker base image

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run tests
        run: npm test

      - name: Build Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: false           # Change to true if you want to push automatically
          tags: myregistry/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Push Docker image
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          docker push myregistry/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}
```

> *Make sure you store your Docker Hub credentials (`DOCKERHUB_USERNAME`, `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN`) as repository secrets.*

---

## 3️⃣ Stage All Changes

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & Push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

> If you’re on a different branch, replace `main` with your branch name.

---

### Quick Summary of What You Did

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1 | Cloned the repo |
| 2.1 | Created a Dockerfile that builds a lightweight Node.js image |
| 2.2 | Added a Kubernetes deployment + service targeting port 3000 |
| 2.3 | Wrote a GitHub Actions workflow that installs deps, runs tests, builds a Docker image, and optionally pushes it |
| 3 | Staged the new files |
| 4 | Committed and pushed to the remote |

Once you’ve pushed, the GitHub Actions workflow will trigger automatically on the next push to `main`. If you set `push: true` in the workflow, it will also push the Docker image to your registry.  

Let me know if you’d like help setting up the Docker registry credentials or tweaking any of the configurations!
